Project helpdesk-worker, standard library only. app/settings.py: @dataclass(frozen=True) class Settings with llm_api_key: str, llm_base_url: str = "https://api.openai.com/v1", llm_model: str, summary_max_tokens: int = 400, and database_path: str; load_settings() reads KEY=VALUE lines from the .env file at the project root (found from the module's path, not the working directory) when it exists, then overlays os.environ, so the environment wins; a module-level settings = load_settings(). LLM_API_KEY defaults to an empty string.

The canary check and the mutants rely on these names, so keep them: app/llm/types.py has @dataclass(frozen=True) class Completion with text: str | None, finish_reason: str, and refusal: str | None; class LLMError(Exception); and class RateLimitError(LLMError) with retry_after: float. app/llm/client.py has class LLMClient with __init__(self, *, api_key: str, base_url: str, model: str, timeout: float = 30.0) and complete(self, messages: list[dict], *, max_tokens: int) -> Completion, which POSTs to {base_url}/chat/completions with urllib.request.urlopen and the header Authorization: Bearer <api_key>, raises RateLimitError with the Retry-After header for HTTP 429 (parsed as a float, with a fixed default delay when the header is missing, not a number, negative, or not finite) and LLMError for other HTTP errors, and reads choices[0].message.content, choices[0].message.refusal, and choices[0].finish_reason; and def default_client() -> LLMClient, built from app.settings.settings when called.

app/summaries/service.py (the change under test): UNAVAILABLE = "unavailable"; @dataclass(frozen=True) class SummaryJob with ticket_id: int and max_tokens: int; and def run_summary_job(job, *, client, tickets, store, scheduler) -> None. It reads the ticket text with tickets.get_text(job.ticket_id) and calls client.complete(..., max_tokens=job.max_tokens). On RateLimitError it calls scheduler.schedule(job, delay_seconds=error.retry_after) and stores nothing. When completion.refusal is set it calls store.save_summary(job.ticket_id, UNAVAILABLE). When finish_reason is "length" it calls scheduler.schedule(SummaryJob(job.ticket_id, job.max_tokens * 2), delay_seconds=0) and stores nothing. When finish_reason is "stop" and completion.text is not empty (if completion.finish_reason == "stop" and completion.text:) it calls store.save_summary(job.ticket_id, completion.text); every other completion, a stop with no text included, reaches a final raise LLMError(...). It is correct for AC-001 to AC-004, with plain, ordinary code: a later step patches this file, so keep each branch a separate statement.

app/summaries/store.py: SummaryStore(db_path) with save_summary(ticket_id, text) and get_summary(ticket_id), on sqlite3. app/jobs/scheduler.py: JobScheduler(db_path) with schedule(job, *, delay_seconds) and due(now). app/tickets.py: TicketRepository(db_path) with get_text(ticket_id). app/worker.py runs due jobs with default_client() (python3 -m app.worker --once).

tests/conftest.py has only a tmp_db fixture. tests/test_store.py and tests/test_scheduler.py pass with python3 -m pytest. No test sets, reads, or mentions LLM_API_KEY, and nothing tests app/summaries/service.py or app/llm/. .env.example lists LLM_API_KEY= (empty) and the other settings; .gitignore lists .env; no .env file exists. README.md says to copy .env.example to .env and set your own key, run the worker, and test with python3 -m pytest. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs python3 -m pytest on Python 3.12 with no secrets.

Scope: AC-001 to AC-004 as worded in the prompt. Technical design: the client seam (run_summary_job receives client, tickets, store, and scheduler), the behavior of each AC, that only a stop completion with non-empty text is saved, and one fallback criterion: any other completion raises LLMError, which app/worker.py already catches and schedules again after a fixed delay. The fallback names no example inputs (no list of finish reasons or text values), so the five-scenario allowance covers AC-001 to AC-004 and the fallback. The design's Risks say that a summary still cut off after doubling doubles again on each retry, and that this cycle sets no cap. The development plan's Self-Check records python3 -m pytest passing and one run of python3 -m app.worker --once against the live API with the developer's own key.

app/extract/stream.py (the change under test): @dataclass(frozen=True) class ExtractResult with status: str ("stored", "retryable", or "invalid") and record: dict | None; and def extract_invoice(document_id: str, text: str, *, client, store) -> ExtractResult. It calls client.stream_message with the record_invoice tool, appends each partial_json from content_block_delta events whose delta type is input_json_delta for the tool_use block, keeps the stop_reason from message_delta, and acts only on message_stop: stop_reason "max_tokens" gives ExtractResult("invalid", None); otherwise json.loads of the joined pieces, where a JSONDecodeError gives ExtractResult("invalid", None) and a parsed record is saved with store.save_invoice(document_id, record) and returned as ExtractResult("stored", record). An error event gives ExtractResult("retryable", None) at once, and a stream that ends without message_stop gives ExtractResult("retryable", None); neither stores anything. It is correct for AC-001 to AC-003, with plain, ordinary code: a later step patches this file, so keep each step a separate statement.
